newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Stocks contribute 0.5 points to Australia GDP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Stocks contribute 0.5 points to Australia GDP.

text.p: Non-farm stocks from selected industries contributed 0.5 percentage points to September quarter growth in Australian gross domestic product, Australian Bureau of Statistics data shows.
Since economists typically expected a detraction from growth of 0.4 percentage points, the figures imply great strengthening in the outlook for September quarter GDP.
Further, the contribution to growth from December quarter stocks has been drastically revised up -- by 0.8 percentage points from minus 0.9 percentage points to minus 0.1 points.
The two more recent quarters have each been slightly revised -- the March quarter contribution has strengthened by 0.1 percentage point while the June quarter weakens by 0.1 point.
The outlook for annual GDP growth has therefore risen even without the unexpected strength of the September quarter contribution.
The bureau's data shows that selected industries' stocks accumulated by A$1.407 billion in the September quarter, compared with A$855 million in the June quarter.
The rise in this rate of accumulation -- A$552 million -- is the 0.5 percentage point contribution to quarterly GDP growth.

The December quarter's big upward revision was balanced by a 1.0 percentage point negative revision in the preceding September quarter, which will not form part of the annual estimates issued in the GDP data due on Wednesday.

The stocks data is a component of expenditure-based estimates of GDP (GDP-E), which are averaged with estimates based on income (GDP-I) and production (GDP-P) to produce GDP-A, the focus of economic policy.
The following table gives economists' typical September quarter forecasts expressed as contributions to quarterly GDP growth and updated with today's data.
Where economists disagree, the figure shown is an average.
